## B Prison Policies

### 1 Stacked Bar Chart - Exclude IDK
Setup for reports that include IDK as middle value
```{r}

# Six individual policies coded 1–4
four_vars <- c(
  "min_wage",
  "free_calls",
  "ed_funds",
  "alt_sentencing",
  "dpen_rev",
  "lwop_rev"
)

# Two voting-rights policies coded 1–2
vote_vars <- c(
  "post_felony_vote_rev",
  "jail_access_rev"
)

# Two indices, each ranging from 1–4
index_vars <- c(
  "prisonhelp",
  "prisonpen"
)

# Labels for figures
policy_labels <- c(
  min_wage = "Minimum wage",
  free_calls = "Free phone calls",
  ed_funds = "Education funding",
  alt_sentencing = "Alternative sentencing",
  dpen_rev = "Death penalty",
  lwop_rev = "Life without parole",
  prisonhelp = "Help index",
  prisonpen = "Punishment index",
  post_felony_vote_rev = "Voting rights after felony conviction",
  jail_access_rev = "Voting access while in jail"
)

# Create folder for figures
dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE,
           recursive = TRUE)

```

####  Response Percentages

```{r}

policy_dist <- sample %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(four_vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "response"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(response), response %in% 1:4) %>%
  count(variable, response, name = "n") %>%
  complete(
    variable = four_vars,
    response = 1:4,
    fill = list(n = 0)
  ) %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  mutate(
    N = sum(n),
    pct = 100 * n / N
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Check the resulting percentages
policy_dist


```



```{r}
policy_dist <- policy_dist %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  mutate(
    p1 = pct[response == 1],
    p2 = pct[response == 2],
    p3 = pct[response == 3],
    p4 = pct[response == 4],

    xmin = case_when(
      response == 1 ~ -(p1 + p2),
      response == 2 ~ -p2,
      response == 3 ~ 0,
      response == 4 ~ p3
    ),

    xmax = case_when(
      response == 1 ~ -p2,
      response == 2 ~ 0,
      response == 3 ~ p3,
      response == 4 ~ p3 + p4
    ),

    y = match(variable, rev(four_vars))
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Labels with sample sizes
policy_ns <- policy_dist %>%
  distinct(variable, N)

axis_labels_A <- paste0(
  unname(policy_labels[rev(four_vars)]),
  " (n = ",
  policy_ns$N[match(rev(four_vars), policy_ns$variable)],
  ")"
)

## Create figure

plot_A <- ggplot(policy_dist) +

  geom_rect(
    aes(
      xmin = xmin,
      xmax = xmax,
      ymin = y - 0.35,
      ymax = y + 0.35,
      fill = factor(response, levels = 1:4)
    ),
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +

  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    color = "grey30",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "1" = "#B35806",
      "2" = "#F1A340",
      "3" = "#92C5DE",
      "4" = "#2166AC"
    ),
    labels = c(
      "Strongly oppose",
      "Somewhat oppose",
      "Somewhat support",
      "Strongly support"
    ),
    name = NULL
  ) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(-100, -50, 0, 50, 100),
    labels = c("100", "50", "0", "50", "100"),
    limits = c(-100, 100)
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq_along(four_vars),
    labels = axis_labels_A,
    expand = expansion(add = 0.6)
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Distribution of policy preferences",
    subtitle = "Opposition (left) and support (right)",
    x = "Percentage of valid responses",
    y = NULL,
    caption = paste(
      "Percentages exclude missing and uncertain responses.",
      "Sample sizes vary by policy due to skipped questions and responses of unsure/no opinion."
    )
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +

  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(color = "black"),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
  )

# Display in R
plot_A

# Export to Overleaf
ggsave(
  "figures/option_A_policy_distribution.pdf",
  plot = plot_A,
  width = 9,
  height = 5.2,
  units = "in"
)
```

### 2. Mean and SD figure - Exclude IDK

```{r}
# Items and indices to include
plot_order <- c(index_vars, four_vars)

summary_B <- sample %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(plot_order)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%

  # Individual items must have responses 1, 2, 3, 4
  # Indices can contain decimals between 1 and 4
  filter(
    !is.na(value),
    if_else(
      variable %in% four_vars,
      value %in% 1:4,
      value >= 1 & value <= 4
    )
  ) %>%

  group_by(variable) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean = mean(value),
    sd = sd(value),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%

  mutate(
    type = if_else(
      variable %in% index_vars,
      "Index",
      "Individual item"
    ),
    variable = factor(
      variable,
      levels = rev(plot_order)
    )
  )

# Inspect before graphing
summary_B
```
#### Mean Panel
```{r}
# Labels with sample sizes
axis_labels_B <- paste0(
  unname(policy_labels[rev(plot_order)]),
  " (n = ",
  summary_B$n[
    match(rev(plot_order),
          as.character(summary_B$variable))
  ],
  ")"
)

names(axis_labels_B) <- rev(plot_order)

# Common appearance
theme_B <- theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(color = "black"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

plot_mean <- ggplot(
  summary_B,
  aes(x = mean, y = variable)
) +

  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 2.5,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "grey70"
  ) +

  geom_point(
    aes(shape = type, color = type),
    size = 3.2
  ) +

  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c(
      "Individual item" = 16,
      "Index" = 18
    )
  ) +

  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Individual item" = "#303D43",
      "Index" = "#2166AC"
    )
  ) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(1, 4, 0.5),
    limits = c(1, 4)
  ) +

  scale_y_discrete(
    labels = axis_labels_B
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Average support",
    x = "Mean response (1–4)",
    y = NULL
  ) +

  theme_B

plot_mean
```
vertical daashed line is numberical midpoint, not a response category.

### A. No Opinion Rates

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

dk_items <- c(
  "post_felony_vote_rev",
  "jail_access_rev",
  "min_wage",
  "free_calls",
  "ed_funds",
  "alt_sentencing",
  "dpen_rev",
  "lwop_rev"
)

dk_labels <- c(
  post_felony_vote_rev = "Post-felony voting",
  jail_access_rev = "Voting access in jail",
  min_wage = "Minimum wage",
  free_calls = "Free phone calls",
  ed_funds = "Education funding",
  alt_sentencing = "Alternative sentencing",
  dpen_rev = "Death penalty policy",
  lwop_rev = "Life without parole policy"
)

dk_groups <- c(
  post_felony_vote_rev = "Voting rights",
  jail_access_rev = "Voting rights",
  min_wage = "Help policies",
  free_calls = "Help policies",
  ed_funds = "Help policies",
  alt_sentencing = "Help policies",
  dpen_rev = "Punishment policies",
  lwop_rev = "Punishment policies"
)

# Check all columns exist
stopifnot(all(
  c(dk_items, paste0("dk_", dk_items)) %in% names(sample)
))

# Create long dataset with one row per person-policy
dk_long <- bind_rows(
  lapply(dk_items, function(v) {
    tibble(
      policy = v,
      score = sample[[v]],
      dk = sample[[paste0("dk_", v)]]
    )
  })
) %>%
  mutate(
    status = case_when(
      dk == 1 ~ "No opinion",
      dk == 0 & !is.na(score) ~ "Substantive",
      TRUE ~ "Unobserved"
    )
  )
```

```{r}
dk_policy_summary <- dk_long %>%
  group_by(policy) %>%
  summarise(
    n_substantive = sum(status == "Substantive"),
    n_dk = sum(status == "No opinion"),
    n_unobserved = sum(status == "Unobserved"),

    n_observed = n_substantive + n_dk,

    pct_dk = if_else(
      n_observed > 0,
      100 * n_dk / n_observed,
      NA_real_
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    policy = factor(policy, levels = rev(dk_items)),
    group = factor(
      unname(dk_groups[as.character(policy)]),
      levels = c(
        "Voting rights",
        "Help policies",
        "Punishment policies"
      )
    )
  )

dk_policy_summary
```
dot plot

```{r}
plot_dk_A <- ggplot(
  dk_policy_summary,
  aes(x = pct_dk, y = policy)
) +

  geom_segment(

    ),

  ) +

    )
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +

  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(color = "black"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
  )

plot_dk_A

ggsave(
  "figures/policy_no_opinion_rates.pdf",
  plot = plot_dk_A,
  width = 9,
  height = 5.5
)
```
### B. Respondent-Level Distribution of No-Opinion Responses (skip for now)

For each respondent, horizontal axis should represent how many of the eight policy questions have observed responses. The vertical axis represents how many received a no-opinion response. Each cell reports the number of respondents with that combination.

What this addresses: someone choosing no opinion on two out of two observed items is not equivalent to someone choosing no opinion on two out of eight.

```{r}

#Check- start
# Which indicators were included?
dk_all_vars
length(dk_all_vars)

# How many items were observed per respondent?
table(sample$dk_answered_all, useNA = "ifany")

# How many no-opinion answers per respondent?
table(sample$dk_total_all, useNA = "ifany")

# Check the distribution jointly
sample %>%
  count(dk_answered_all, dk_total_all) %>%
  arrange(dk_answered_all, dk_total_all)
#Check- end

# recalc start
dk_eight_vars <- c(
  "dk_post_felony_vote_rev",
  "dk_jail_access_rev",
  "dk_min_wage",
  "dk_free_calls",
  "dk_ed_funds",
  "dk_alt_sentencing",
  "dk_dpen_rev",
  "dk_lwop_rev"
)

dk_person <- sample %>%
  mutate(
    n_observed_8 = rowSums(
      !is.na(pick(all_of(dk_eight_vars)))
    ),

    n_dk_8 = rowSums(
      pick(all_of(dk_eight_vars)) == 1,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    prop_dk_8 = if_else(
      n_observed_8 > 0,
      n_dk_8 / n_observed_8,
      NA_real_
    )
  )

# Inspect the new variables
table(dk_person$n_observed_8, useNA = "ifany")
table(dk_person$n_dk_8, useNA = "ifany")

summary(dk_person$prop_dk_8)

# recalc end

# new chart code

dk_frequency <- dk_person %>%
  filter(n_observed_8 == 8) %>%
  count(n_dk_8, name = "respondents") %>%
  complete(
    n_dk_8 = 0:8,
    fill = list(respondents = 0)
  )

plot_dk_B <- ggplot(
  dk_frequency,
  aes(x = n_dk_8, y = respondents)
) +

  geom_col(
    fill = "#4477AA",
    width = 0.7
  ) +

  geom_text(
    aes(label = respondents),
    vjust = -0.5,
    size = 3.5
  ) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 0:8
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Distribution of no-opinion responses",
    subtitle = "Respondents with eight observed policy responses",
    x = "Number of policies answered 'no opinion'",
    y = "Number of respondents"
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +

  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

plot_dk_B


ggsave(
  "figures/respondent_dk_distribution.pdf",
  plot = plot_dk_B,
  width = 7.5,
  height = 6
)

```

### C. Response Status Composition

```{r}

dk_status_summary <- dk_long %>%
  count(policy, status, name = "n") %>%
  group_by(policy) %>%
  mutate(
    pct = 100 * n / sum(n)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    policy = factor(
      policy,
      levels = rev(dk_items)
    ),
    status = factor(
      status,
      levels = c(
        "Substantive",
        "No opinion",
        "Unobserved"
      )
    )
  )

plot_dk_C <- ggplot(
  dk_status_summary,
  aes(x = policy, y = pct, fill = status)
) +

  scale_x_discrete(
    labels = function(x) unname(dk_labels[x])

    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
```

## Prison Voting Policies

###  Stacked - Exclude IDKs
```{r}
vote_summary <- sample %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(vote_vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "response"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(response), response %in% c(1, 2)) %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    pct_support = 100 * mean(response == 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    variable = factor(
      variable,
      levels = rev(vote_vars)
    )
  )

plot_vote <- ggplot(
  vote_summary,
  aes(x = pct_support, y = variable)
) +

  geom_col(
    fill = "#2166AC",
    width = 0.55
  ) +

  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = sprintf(
        "%.1f%% (n = %s)",
        pct_support, n
      )
    ),
    hjust = 1.05,
    color = "white",
    size = 3.5
  ) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 100),
    breaks = seq(0, 100, 25),
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")
  ) +

  scale_y_discrete(
    labels = function(x) unname(policy_labels[x])
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Support for voting-rights policies",
    x = "Percentage supporting",
    y = NULL
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +

  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(color = "black"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

plot_vote

ggsave(
  "figures/voting_rights_support.pdf",
  plot = plot_vote,
  width = 8,
  height = 3,
  units = "in"
)
```

## B All Policy Means x Impact - Version 1

Grouped by help, pun, etc.

```{r}



sample %>%
  dplyr::group_by(impact) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    dpen_rev = mean(dpen_rev, na.rm = TRUE),
    lwop_rev = mean(lwop_rev, na.rm = TRUE),
    prisonpen   = mean(prisonpen, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

help_means_impact <- (sample %>%
  dplyr::group_by(impact) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(

get_means <- function(var) {
  sample %>%
    dplyr::filter(.data[[var]] %in% c(0, 1)) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(.data[[var]]) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      dplyr::across(

      ),

    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(group = var) %>%
    dplyr::rename(value = all_of(var)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(row = paste0(group, " = ", value)) %>%
    dplyr::select(row, all_of(policy_vars))
}
```

```{r}
#defining the non impact means and percent differences from impact vars
pct_diff <- function(x, ref) {
  ((x - ref) / ref) * 100
}

policy_summary <- function(df, var) {

  no_impact_mean <- mean(
    df[[var]][df$impact == 0],
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

  impact_mean <- mean(
    df[[var]][df$impact == 1],
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

  direct_mean <- mean(
    df[[var]][df$incarc == 1],
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

  proximal_mean <- mean(
    df[[var]][df$knowincarc == 1],
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

  victim_mean <- mean(
    df[[var]][df$vict == 1],
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

  tibble::tibble(
    var = var,
    no_impact_mean = no_impact_mean,
    impact_diff = mean_diff(impact_mean, no_impact_mean),
    direct_diff = mean_diff(direct_mean, no_impact_mean),
    proximal_diff = mean_diff(proximal_mean, no_impact_mean),
    victim_diff = mean_diff(victim_mean, no_impact_mean)
  )
}


## old p val 

pval_ttest <- function(df, var, group_var) {
  sub <- df %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[var]]), !is.na(.data[[group_var]])) %>%
    dplyr::filter(.data[[group_var]] %in% c(0, 1))

  if (length(unique(sub[[group_var]])) < 2) return(NA_real_)

  stats::t.test(sub[[var]] ~ sub[[group_var]])$p.value
}

add_star <- function(x, p) {
  ifelse(!is.na(p) & p < .05, paste0(sprintf("%.1f", x), "*"), sprintf("%.1f", x))
}

    ),
    
    p_victim = purrr::map_dbl(

      ~ pval_ttest(sample, .x, "vict")
    )
  )

# Mean differences relative to respondents reporting
# none of the three focal experiences
mean_diff <- function(x, ref) {
  x - ref
}

policy_summary <- function(df, var) {
  no_impact_mean <- mean(df[[var]][df$impact == 0], na.rm = TRUE)
  impact_mean <- mean(df[[var]][df$impact == 1], na.rm = TRUE)
  direct_mean    <- mean(df[[var]][df$incarc == 1], na.rm = TRUE)
  proximal_mean  <- mean(df[[var]][df$knowincarc == 1], na.rm = TRUE)
  victim_mean    <- mean(df[[var]][df$vict == 1], na.rm = TRUE)
  
  tibble::tibble(
    var = var,
    no_impact_mean = no_impact_mean,
    impact_mean = pct_diff(impact_mean, no_impact_mean),
    direct_pct = pct_diff(direct_mean, no_impact_mean),
    proximal_pct = pct_diff(proximal_mean, no_impact_mean),
    victim_pct = pct_diff(victim_mean, no_impact_mean)
  )
}

policy_table <- purrr::map_dfr(
  policy_map$var,
  ~ policy_summary(sample, .x)
) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(policy_map, by = "var") %>%
  dplyr::select(
    var, section, label,
    no_impact_mean,
    impact_mean,
    direct_diff,
    proximal_diff,
    victim_diff
  )

pval_ttest <- function(df, var, group_var) {
  sub <- df %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      !is.na(.data[[var]]),
      !is.na(.data[[group_var]])
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(.data[[group_var]] %in% c(0, 1))
  
  if (length(unique(sub[[group_var]])) < 2) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  
  stats::t.test(
    sub[[var]] ~ sub[[group_var]]
  )$p.value
}

add_star <- function(x, p) {
  formatted <- sprintf("%+.2f", x)
  
  ifelse(
    !is.na(p) & p < .05,
    paste0(formatted, "*"),
    formatted
  )
}

policy_stars <- policy_map %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    p_direct = purrr::map_dbl(
      var,
      ~ pval_ttest(
        sample %>%
          dplyr::filter(impact == 0 | incarc == 1),
        .x,
        "incarc"
      )
    ),
    
    p_proximal = purrr::map_dbl(
      var,
      ~ pval_ttest(
        sample %>%
          dplyr::filter(impact == 0 | knowincarc == 1),
        .x,
        "knowincarc"
      )
    ),
    
    p_victim = purrr::map_dbl(
      var,
      ~ pval_ttest(
        sample %>%
          dplyr::filter(impact == 0 | vict == 1),
        .x,
        "vict"
      )
    )
  )

policy_table_final <- policy_table %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    policy_stars %>%
      dplyr::select(var, p_direct, p_proximal, p_victim),
    by = "var"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    no_impact_mean   = sprintf("%.2f", no_impact_mean),
    direct_display   = add_star(direct_diff, p_direct),
    proximal_display = add_star(proximal_diff, p_proximal),
    victim_display   = add_star(victim_diff, p_victim)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    section,
    label,
    no_impact_mean,
    direct_display,
    proximal_display,
    victim_display
  )

View(policy_table_final)
```

## B All Policy Means x Impact - Version 2

```{r}


library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)

# -----------------------------------------
# 1. Define the eight individual policies
# -----------------------------------------

policy_items <- c(
  "min_wage",
  "free_calls",
  "ed_funds",
  "alt_sentencing",
  "dpen_rev",
  "lwop_rev",
  "post_felony_vote_rev",
  "jail_access_rev"
)

# -----------------------------------------
# 2. Define the six groups
# -----------------------------------------

policy_groups <- list(
  "Full sample" = sample,

  "No experience" = sample %>%
    filter(impact == 0),

  "Any experience" = sample %>%
    filter(impact == 1),

  "Incarcerated" = sample %>%
    filter(incarc == 1),

  "Proximal" = sample %>%
    filter(knowincarc == 1),

  "Victimized" = sample %>%
    filter(vict == 1)
)

# -----------------------------------------
# 3. Calculate statistics for each group
# -----------------------------------------

policy_stats <- purrr::imap_dfr(
  policy_groups,
  function(df, group_label) {

    df %>%
      dplyr::select(all_of(policy_items)) %>%
      pivot_longer(
        cols = everything(),
        names_to = "policy",
        values_to = "response"
      ) %>%
      group_by(policy) %>%
      summarise(
        n = sum(!is.na(response)),

        mean = if (n > 0) {
          mean(response, na.rm = TRUE)
        } else NA_real_,

        sd = if (n > 1) {
          sd(response, na.rm = TRUE)
        } else NA_real_,

        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      mutate(group = group_label)
  }
)

# Inspect the long-format results
View(policy_stats)

```

```{r}
policy_table <- policy_stats %>%
  mutate(
    display = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", mean, sd),
    group = factor(
      group,
      levels = names(policy_groups)
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(policy, group, display) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = group,
    values_from = display
  )
```
